title: arXiv Trending AI — Daily | 21 October 2026
global_caveat: arXiv has no official trending chart; this is an inferred ordering based on checkable independent coverage, cross-list breadth, and public project signals. Semantic Scholar citation evidence is limited: all six selected papers currently show zero citations.

sections.title: Agentic World Action Models
sections.abstract: AW-0 jointly generates code-based skill plans, future video, and robot actions, and the paper reports gains over VLA and world-action baselines on simulation and physical manipulation tasks.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors propose AW-0's mixture-of-transformers architecture with coupled code, video, and action streams, plus a pipeline to annotate and consolidate reusable skills; they report improved results on RoboTwin 2.0 and physical bimanual tasks.
sections.unique_caveat: The paper reports AW-0's default success rate falling from 80.8% on clean RoboTwin scenes to 20.6% under visual randomization; hybrid execution raises the randomized result to 29.2% but lowers clean-scene success to 63.1%.
sections.ranking_evidence: Independent technical coverage appeared at AI Weekly; the public repository showed 43 stars when checked.

sections.title: LongZero: Enhancing Long-Context Reasoning in LLMs from Zero Data
sections.abstract: LongZero has an LLM create answer-first, verifiable long-context reasoning and retrieval tasks from its own outputs, then trains on them with GRPO; experiments cover two models and five benchmarks.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors specify questions, evidence, and answers before expanding them into long contexts, combine reasoning with retrieval exercises, and filter tasks by model difficulty; they report higher averages than two RL data-generation baselines on both tested models.
sections.unique_caveat: The authors document that defective generated questions can still pass their filtering; evaluation is limited to two Qwen base models, and reported gains vary by benchmark.
sections.ranking_evidence: Independent summaries at arXivTLDR and Fellow News, cross-listing in two core AI categories, and author-linked code and data.

sections.title: Multimodal Embodied Agents: A Unified Capability-centric Perspective from Computer-Use to Robot-Use
sections.abstract: The survey proposes PAPAV—Perceive, Anticipate, Plan, Act, Verify—to compare multimodal and embodied agents, and audits how 64 benchmarks evaluate these capabilities.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors define a capability-based comparison framework and report that among 64 reviewed benchmarks, 5 explicitly assess Anticipate and 3 assess Verify.
sections.unique_caveat: This is a framework and benchmark review, not a controlled comparison of a new agent; its audit depends on how the authors classify the selected benchmark set.
sections.ranking_evidence: Cross-listed in five configured categories, with a public project/benchmark index and independent AI Weekly coverage.

sections.title: Environment Duels: A Microcosm of LLM Co-Evolution
sections.abstract: Environment Duels evaluates language models as both authors and solvers of interactive tasks, reporting that the two roles differ and that hint lift in one RL study tracks transfer to held-out benchmarks.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors introduce a benchmark in which models create tasks with privileged hints and other models try to solve them, then test whether hint lift predicts downstream RL benefit.
sections.unique_caveat: The reported learning-transfer experiment trains one Qwen3.8-27B learner on environments from four authors; this does not establish that benchmark co-evolution patterns generalize to deployed training pipelines.
sections.ranking_evidence: Searchable code repository, an independent ST-Hakky overview, and cross-listing in two core categories.

sections.title: PhysiCalWorld: In-Context Physics Calibration for World Models
sections.abstract: PhysiCalWorld encodes a short exploratory interaction as a reusable physics descriptor so an action-conditioned world model can adapt predictions to scene-specific dynamics without fine-tuning or physics labels.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report better rollout prediction and visual-planning success across four environments with varied physics, and say the learned descriptors generalize beyond the training physics ranges.
sections.unique_caveat: The authors state that training requires trajectories grouped by physics configuration, calibration depends on the quality of the exploratory prompt, and the method assumes physics remain stationary within an episode.
sections.ranking_evidence: Cross-listed in robotics, AI, and vision and relevant to the world-model/physical-control intersection; independent attention evidence was thinner than for higher-ranked entries.

sections.title: Quant-Arena: Benchmarking LLM Agents for Quantitative Trading Research
sections.abstract: Quant-Arena evaluates whether LLM agents can research and freeze an executable A-share strategy using 2022–2023 feedback, then tests it on a sealed 2024 period with trading costs and market-impact modeling.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors propose an end-to-end benchmark for quantitative research rather than formula or code generation alone, with an out-of-sample assessment under cash-account constraints.
sections.unique_caveat: In the authors' sealed 2024 evaluation, none of the nine tested frontier models beats the equal-weight market; the results are specific to the A-share data and evaluation protocol.
sections.ranking_evidence: Public benchmark and leaderboard plus a Hugging Face paper page; cross-listed in AI and language categories, with limited independent discussion and citation evidence.
